If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently bearish (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.  
For mid-horizon (8–15 days), if sentiment swings from bullish to bearish, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per sentiment reversal.  
For late-horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment remains stable above 0.67, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to reflect sustained bullish momentum.  
If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast shows strong upward trend, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overfitting to recent volatility.  
If sentiment is mixed and forecast shows strong downward trend, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid underestimating market resilience.
